terms.definition: Run the terminology-lookup Tool down the four reuse-first rungs of the terminology-coding methodology: (1) target guide vocabulary, (2) smart-base generic personas, GRADE code lists and guideline-domain glossary, (3) external WHO-FIC/ILO standards (ICD-11, ICHI/CDHIv2, ISCO-08, ATC), (4) local glossary candidate (status: candidate, source: extracted), or could-not-determine for business-process with its WARNING line.

terms.prefLabel: Adjudicate slot codings and glossary candidates
terms.definition: Review each slot's classification and code against the terminology-coding methodology: the authoritative scheme for the slot, the reuse-first rung, skos:exactMatch vs skos:closeMatch precision (ontologist), and any Rung 4 glossary candidates (promote valid ones from candidate to authored per glossary-terms, or replace them with an existing code).

terms.prefLabel: Check exclusions against page and sign
terms.definition: Open library/<doc_id>/sections/page-NNN.md beside exclusions.proposed.json. Read each candidate sentence on the printed page, check that the proposed reason (background-fact, manufacturer-statement, editorial, research-question, duplicate-of) holds without dropping normative guidance, and sign the exclusion (signedOffBy) or reject it with a reason.

terms.definition: Write the candidate codings, provenance bases, warnings report and any unsigned exclusions.proposed.json entries, and request review with deep links to the staged pages and the printed page sections.

DIIG Chapter 4. Select interventions for the prioritized challenges, assess whether the enabling environment can support them, identify functional requirements and user stories, map the future-state workflow, and check whether existing applications already meet the requirements. The interventions CONSIDERED AND NOT CHOSEN are part of the output, with why — `methodology-adoption`'s fourth refusal. A deleted alternative leaves the next reader unable to tell a decision from an oversight. Selection is from the Classification, and the `who-digital-health` voice governs the naming: an intervention is a capability, not the software that delivers it.

DIIG Chapter 7. Phases of implementation, cost drivers, and the budget matrix. This is the chapter that turns the preceding six into a COSTED implementation plan, which is the artefact the whole Guide exists to produce and the one a funder reads.

terms.prefLabel: Form the team and establish goals
terms.definition: DIIG Chapter 2. Determine roles and responsibilities; develop a common understanding of the health programme's needs and goals; understand programme operations across levels of the health system.

DIIG Chapter 6. Assess the digital health enterprise architecture, identify the common and enabling components and shared services that make up the digital health platform, and link the investment to both.

terms.prefLabel: Map the current state and confirm bottlenecks
terms.definition: DIIG Chapter 3.1. Determine the health programme processes to target, map their workflows, identify and confirm bottlenecks. Then 3.2, a root cause analysis. This is where DIIG builds on CRDM, and it says so: "This process builds on the Public Health Informatics Institute's Collaborative Requirements Development Methodology (CRDM)". Its three areas of concentration are business process analysis, business process redesign and requirements definition — two of which name diagrams this platform already executes. They are parallel tracks, not a composite: pick one per decision and name it.

DIIG Chapter 8. Establish a logic model, plan the monitoring and evaluation, establish a culture of data use, and manage adaptively — using the data to optimize the interventions rather than only to report on them. The full treatment of this chapter is a separate publication in this library, `9789241511766-eng`, Monitoring and Evaluating Digital Health Interventions. It is a parallel track, not a sub-step: do not blend the two.

DIIG Chapter 5. Infrastructure; legislation, policy and compliance, including data management, privacy and security, and the regulation of new technologies; leadership and governance, including external partnerships; workforce and training; services and applications.

terms.prefLabel: Prioritize, and map to health system challenges
terms.definition: DIIG Chapters 3.3 and 3.4. Prioritize the bottlenecks, then map the programme-specific ones onto the generic health system challenges. THE ARITHMETIC IS REFUSED HERE. DIIG Table 3.3.1 asks three questions, each scored 1-3 — how much impact does this bottleneck have on the process, what is the likelihood of overcoming it, is it important to a wide range of stakeholders — and sums them into a Score and a Prioritized Ranking. The three criteria are adopted whole; the total is not. Record each criterion's answer AND its reason, and order by argument. A ranked list reads as evidence in a way three stated judgements do not, and the weights were invented.

terms.prefLabel: Make the value proposition and set next steps
terms.definition: DIIG Chapter 9. The case made to whoever pays, and what follows. Scaling up is a different method and a different publication — `9789241509510-eng`, The MAPS Toolkit — which begins where this implementation ends.

cat-harness's generic review, called: classify what changed, review it, and record a qa-review/v1 QaReview whose subject is the component and whose Decision carries the reviewing role. The reviewer reads the staged page and the before/after; for a figure or table, the visual-diff picture and its changed-pixel count; for a form, the wireframe (wireframe-design-review; at L3 its Questionnaire follows fhir-questionnaire-wireframe). What to judge per component is in the skill's column "the reviewer judges".

The mechanical checks for this component, before anyone is asked (skill l2-component-edit-review, column "checker"): BPMN imports in bpmn-js with no warnings and its lanes map to personas (dak-swimlanes.ts); DMN loads, its decisions are reachable (artefact-reachability, audit:reachability) and its test cases run (content-test); the data dictionary web annex's ids are unique and its references and terminology bindings resolve (check-web-annexes.ts); personas, scenarios and requirements each trace to an L1 recommendation (recommendation-extraction's implementedBy edges). Findings go with the review request; a failing check does not stop the hand-on.

Create or change the component with the authoring skill the call names, one component per pass. On rework, apply the review's findings; a fix written in an AuditNote is applied as given. An adapted component is edited against its pinned upstream, so the before side of the diff is that upstream, not an empty file.

Render the component the way its reviewer reads it (column "renderer and diff"): the BPMN diagram (render:bpmn) with a visual-diff picture; the DMN decision table (smart-base-transform.py dmn2html) with each rule's L1 citation; the data dictionary's term diff (dak-data-dictionary-diff.ts) and the chosen wireframe of each form; personas, scenarios and requirements as a prose diff. Commit to the feature branch so it is staged as branches/<slug>/ on the platform's just-the-docs site (for smart-base, a folio-assistant staging re-pin, never the IG's /deploy), and make the before/after preview here so it exists when review starts.

File a bean against the stage that chose the rejected source or dependency (check for an existing one first), and mark every asset derived from this component adjudication: rejected-upstream on its wasDerivedFrom edge. Nothing is deleted: the re-derivation may come out the same.

terms.prefLabel: Ask for review with staging deep links
terms.definition: Ask the person in the reviewing role, following staging-review's deep-link rule: one deep link per changed page and anchor on branches/<slug>/, each beside the same page on main (or "new page"), the pages taken from the change (rendered-impact); say so if there is no preview yet. Lead with what changed in prose, then the links, the before/after and the checker's findings; put the question in interaction-modality's form. Post it where the work is discussed (this conversation, the originating GitHub issue, the pull request), with the same links in each. A comment tagged on the PR becomes a review-comment todo (review-comments).

Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the BPMN inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: bpmn-js import with no warnings, dak-swimlanes.ts, artefact-reachability; renderer: render:bpmn with a visual-diff before/after; reviewer: clinical SME).

terms.definition: Author the data dictionary and core data elements: structured but not FHIR, reviewable by a clinician, so L3 can be derived from them rather than written twice. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the glossary inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: check-web-annexes.ts on the data dictionary web annex; renderer: the term diff from dak-data-dictionary-diff.ts and each form's chosen wireframe; reviewer: clinical SME, terminologist for codes).

Author the decision and scheduling logic as DMN tables within the FEEL subset the interpreter implements (any, literals, comparisons, one-of); ranges, not() and function calls are refused at load. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the DMN inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: load, reachability, test cases; renderer: dmn2html table before/after, each rule beside its L1 citation; reviewer: clinical SME).

Author the indicators and the functional and non-functional requirements. These are the DAK's requirements, not skills/requirements/*.json (this harness's own conformance obligations). Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the indicators-and-requirements inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: each names the persona and process it serves and traces to L1; renderer: prose diff; reviewer: business analyst with the programme manager).

terms.prefLabel: Build the L1 library from Component 1
terms.definition: Ingest the DAK into the library; it is L2, so it gets no L1 graph. Read Component 1 §1.2 for its sources (extract-dak-l1-references.ts --context-only), fetch each L1 source (fetch-dspace-item.ts for an IRIS handle, fetch-who-publication.ts for a who.int item page) and ingest it. Record on its intake whether each is L1 (declared > context > inferred; --record-context writes §1.2's context). For each L1 source, run l1-specialise.ts: its publication, sections and elements as specialisations of its library nodes, since the library is upstream of L1. Validate with the smart-base Zod validator. Citation fidelity (does each citation name the source it resolves to) and a cited edition older than the one fetched are left to a person, never passed automatically.

Author the DAK's personas and the user scenarios they appear in. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the personas-and-scenarios inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: dak-swimlanes.ts and traceability to L1 recommendations; renderer: the persona card and a prose diff; reviewer: clinical SME). These are the DAK's own actors, not this harness's scenarios/roles.json; do not conflate the two.
Enumerate the processes, decisions and data elements the guideline implies; identify the actors.

Turn the scope into child beans of the DAK's bean, one per DAK component: the DAK's work plan holds the work plan of each component. beans create is not idempotent: check for an existing bean before every create, or a re-run duplicates the plan.

Ground truth: does the DAK say what the guideline says? The whole-DAK reading across components: whether personas, processes, decisions, data elements and indicators tell one consistent story. Per-component reviews already happened inside each track (Process_L2ComponentEditReview) and are not repeated.

ICD-11, SNOMED CT and LOINC bindings, governed separately from the artefacts that cite them. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the terminology inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: bindings resolve and unmappedConcepts is reported; renderer: the term diff on the code columns; reviewer: a terminologist other than the one who bound it).

Against the stage-6 IG build, with conformance tests from the IG's examples and test cases.

From the L1 KG: which existing DAKs to reuse, adapt, extend or reject, each with evidence and reason. Reuse first; prefer the jurisdiction's adaptation, recording the WHO original as its upstream. For each component kept, record how the candidate produces it (the tools graph, the candidate repository's source spreadsheets and converters, WHO's DAK toolchain); stage 4 uses that toolchain.

Who uses it, on what device, which L2 processes and L3 resources it covers, connectivity, the systems it talks to. The agent offers options drawn from the L2 personas and processes. This is the written intent wireframe-design-review starts from.
Population, setting, jurisdiction, interventions in scope. The user's own words; the agent asks a numbered question if the request did not say.
Component 1 sources of any DAK already in scope first, then WHO IRIS and the jurisdiction's own guidelines. Each candidate marked in-library / in-KG / not yet.

Per source not yet extracted: cat ingest into library/, the generic-document layer (l1-library), then the L1 layer (recommendations, remarks, practices, scenario candidates) into library/<bib>/l1-extraction/.

The authoring steps of l2-dak-authoring.bpmn (personas and scenarios, BPMN, DMN, data dictionary, indicators and requirements, terminology), plus the design of each data-entry form as wireframe candidates (wireframe-design-review, design use) from the persona, the user scenario and the core data elements. Its clinical validation is this stage's adjudication and does not hold up stage 5. The IG is built through fhir-harness's AST cache lifecycle (ig-ast-refresh.yml), with the DAK pre-processing as smart-base's pre-export overlay (dak-preprocessing, dak-pre-export.sh) and the DAK sidecars made from the AST (dak-postprocessing).

The mapping and pipeline of dak-l3-ig.bpmn, up to a clean IG build. Every L3 asset names the L2 asset it implements in wasDerivedFrom, with that edge's adjudication state. Each Questionnaire is derived from the chosen L2 wireframe of its form. Publication continues in that process and is not on the path to stage 8.

The order rule as a check with its own contract (skill l3-readiness). Every source has its L1 extraction, every L2 asset names an L1 node, every L3 artefact about to be written names its L2 asset, and the review of each extraction and L2 asset has been requested. Returns ready and the findings, each with the stage that fixes it.

To-be mode, from the stage-7 intent: two or more candidates, web and mobile, with real content from the L2 personas and scenarios. The agent goes on with its recommended candidate; the requester may choose another during adjudication.
